observations: 53 of 104 crates (51%) sit before the vine: the first act teaches crates, later acts use 3-10 per section.
Teaching order: plain crate -> crab -> hidden crate behind a jumped wall (#8) -> TNT with prompt -> TNT triangle -> Aku -> checkpoint -> stack -> 15-crate exit wall.
The first count trap (crate 8) sits behind the low wall you just jumped, before the player cares about the all-box gem.
Protection before danger and saves after it: Aku at the foot of the spider temple, C1 at the top of its stairs; every checkpoint follows a new hazard.
The biggest cluster (15) is the temple exit itself, so every player sees unsupported crates settle.
Forced-motion vine: the first crate is beside the line at ride height (collects itself), the rest float one jump above it.
Enemies set the timing, not the location: crates sit in throwers' lanes and spiders' drop zones.
Bait clusters sit at bonus pads, bonus exits and the final summit, where attention is pulled to a goal.
No Nitro, !, iron-bound or bounce crate; the only tool crate (arrow) is in the death-free bonus.
The all-box goal costs only two deliberate turn-backs (#8 and the pad pair).

geometryObservations: Every traversal verb is taught on non-lethal geometry with a prompt: JUMP on a 0.5-1 u railed step (G-S1-a), DOUBLE JUMP up a 2-3 u dead-end wall (G-S2-b), CRAWL under the gem hut (G-S4-b), the held bounce in the bonus (G-B-b). Lethal gaps only follow once the verb exists.

The first forced lethal gap comes ~ 80 s in (temple pillars, G-S2-a): a standing jump of ~ 1.5-2 u onto a ~ 2 u round top. S1 has no forced pit: its floor hole (G-S1-b) lies beside the line and the arch bridge is a 2 u lane with a curb.
Gap widths barely change (1.5-3 u all level); difficulty grows through smaller landings (hub -> 2 u tops -> crate-occupied tops -> 2 u skulls), platform timers and enemies placed on landings.

Timers arrive in the second half: sinking blocks (S5) after ~ 2.5 min of static ground, crumbling skulls (S8) for the finale. Each timed crossing ends on a checkpoint floor (C3 landing) or the summit.

One enemy type per biome: crabs on the beach and path, spiders in the temple and cave, throwers on the vine and in the village, plants on the wall. Each type first appears in a harmless form: the hub crab alone, spider puddles before the spider, the vine thrower out of reach before the village throwers.
Telegraphs are physical and early: green puddles mark spider drops, the wheels are seen rolling in on a curved causeway, the plants live in visible holes.
There is only one dedicated timed hazard (the rolling wheels). It sits between the two TNT lessons, so the player never times a hazard and handles an explosive at once.
Rest floors bracket every challenge: courtyard (C1), chamber, C2 deck, C3 landing, cave floor (C4), wall base (C5), summit. No two hazard groups touch.
The vine is a no-fail ride (GP) in the middle of the level: a rhythm break between the temple enemies and the village throwers, with crate hops as optional timing.
Camera changes mark new grammar: side-scroll for the bonus pillars, a side view for the climb so tiers ~ 2 u apart can be read, a chase camera for the vine.

Enemies sit on landings and next to required actions: a spider over the pillar landing (G-S2-a), a spider over the TNT (S2-c), plants under climb ledges. The "do two things at once" pairing is introduced one pair at a time.
The bonus has the hardest footing (~ 1.5 u pillar tops, a tilted slab) because a fall there costs nothing.
geometryTransfer: First-jump lesson: a 0.6-1.2 m (1/2-1 crate) railed step across the corridor with a prompt and no pit. First lethal gap 1.7-2.3 m (1.5-2 crates) onto round tops 2.3 m across from a standing take-off, about a third of our 5.6 m running jump.

Double-jump wall: a 2.3-3.5 m (2-3 crate) step-up at a corridor dead end with no pit; full jump 2.85 m + double 1.74 m reaches 4.6 m, so a 3-crate face (3.46 m) forces the double jump. Put the crate-wall gate on top.
Sinking crossing: two `crumble` or `phasepad` blocks 2.3-2.9 m square with gaps of 2.3 m -> 3.5 m -> 2.3 m, ~ 1 s per block, ending on a checkpoint floor >= 4.6 m wide.
Spider analogue: a `floater` (no stomp) hanging over a landing pad, with a floor decal under its drop point visible 3-4 s before the player arrives; never over a take-off edge the first time.

Side-view wall climb: ledges 2.3-3.5 m wide at 2.3 m vertical spacing (~ 80 % of the 2.85 m full jump), alternating static slabs and `crumble` skulls so every second or third tier is stable; ambushers in holes under ledges (a `sentry` or plant-like prop); checkpoint at the base.
Timed gate between two explosive lessons: two `stone` boulders crossing a 3.5 m causeway ~ 1 s apart, with no explosive in the boulder lane.
